The selected SLM parameters were a laser power of 300 W, a scanning speed of 1000 mm/s, and a hatch spacing of 0.15 mm. The printing process was conducted under argon gas protection, maintaining a chamber oxygen content below 0.1 %.
solution treatment temperatures of 500 – 600 ◦C (increment of 50 ◦C) were selected with a holding time of 1 h.
the sample hardness reaching a peak value of 135 HV after 2 h of aging. ... the selected aging heat treatment condition was a temperature of 400 ◦C and a time of 2 h.

attributes.location: along grain boundaries in equiaxed grain region

evidence.quote: In the equiaxed grain region, the precipitates appear as long strips distributed along the grain boundaries ... the precipitates in the equiaxed grain region are also Al11Cu5Mn3

attributes.location: in the matrix inside columnar grains

evidence.quote: After aging heat treatment, fine secondary needle-shaped precipitates of Al11Cu5Mn3 were formed in the matrix, while the primary Al11Cu5Mn3 precipitates coarsened and grew.

attributes.location: along grain boundaries in equiaxed grain region

evidence.quote: The precipitates along the grain boundaries experienced significant coarsening, with sizes reaching approximately 500 nm. SAED pattern analysis confirmed that these larger grain boundary precipitates are also Al11Cu5Mn3
A high-resolution TEM image indicates the smaller particle-like precipitates are Al2CuMg, as shown in Fig. 11 (f).
This is mainly due to the aluminum alloy matrix having a face-centered cubic structure, where the growth rate along the < 001 > direction is the fastest

The columnar grain region of the samples before and after heat treatment exhibited a < 001 > preferred orientation
the equiaxed grain regions showed no significant preferred orientation and consisted of single substructured grains
the SLMed alloy exhibits a typical fish-scale structure
black agglomerates are present in the alloy, which are attributed to dislocation tangles caused by the high cooling rate during the printing process
